title: Minimal runtime assurances and staged pinning for third-party model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Community/third-party model submissions are increasingly varied in topology and behavior. Without a small, enforceable set of runtime guarantees and a clear staged pinning approach, we expose customers to silent regressions (latency spikes, OOMs, tokenization mismatches) and operators to unpredictable rollbacks. This PRD defines the minimum runtime assurances required for a new open model to be admitted to the catalog and a staged pinning policy (what to pin, when, and how to relax pins) to minimize production impact.

Goals: (1) Produce a concise checklist of runtime checks that can be executed as part of the intake pipeline (sanity-profiles, perf-bench, tokenizer-agreement). (2) Define a 3-stage pinning path (ephemeral, guarded, pinned) with clear triggers for promotion and rollback. (3) Specify acceptance criteria, observability signals, and developer UX (catalog metadata fields and admin controls) so downstream teams can rely on catalog entries.

Non-goals: This ticket does not mandate specific quantization knobs, nor does it replace deep model safety evaluation or privacy audits. It is focused on runtime compatibility and operational predictability for serving on Redwood Dedicated/Hosted runtimes.
scope_in: Tokenizer round-trip check across reference inputs
Basic KV-cache sanity (no cache corruption across sequences)
Perf profile within host runtime for three canonical sequence lengths (<64, 256, 1024)
Deterministic fallback mapping for unsupported ops (recorded in catalog metadata)
Catalog metadata fields for: recommended pin level, incompatible-kernel-notes, verified-sequence-latency
requirements: Onboarding pipeline adds a 'runtime_assurances' artifact (JSON) per model that includes: tokenizer_hash, perf_profiles, op_compat_warnings
Define three pin states: ephemeral (default for unvetted), guarded (auto-promote candidate after 7 days of steady traffic), pinned (explicit admin pin) and document promotion/rollback hooks
Add two runtime probes in staging: cold-start latency (p50/p95) and memory high-water (RSS/VRAM) for a standard 16-token and 512-token workload
Catalog UI: show 'recommended_pin' and an info link to the intake artifact; admin toggles to override pin and force rollback
Runtime must tag requests that hit fallback kernels and increment a per-model counter visible in Console
acceptance_criteria: A test fixture exists that runs the intake pipeline end-to-end and outputs a runtime_assurances JSON for a sample community model
Automated job in CI that rejects catalog entries if tokenizer_hash mismatches reference tokenization on canonical inputs
Console displays recommended_pin and a single-click flow to escalate from ephemeral -> guarded -> pinned with a recorded audit log entry
Fallback kernel hits are surfaced in model dashboard with a count and last-seen timestamp; if >1% of tokens use fallbacks during the first 48h of traffic the model remains in 'guarded' state
Documentation (confluence) with examples and a migration checklist published and linked from the intake PR template
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement intake artifact and tokenizer round-trip checks; ship CI gate. Phase 2 (3 weeks): add perf probes and Console metadata surface. Phase 3 (1 week): apply staged pinning workflow to a candidate set of 5 community models and monitor signals for 14 days. Post-mortem & recommendations after pilot, then flip catalog admission to require runtime_assurances for new entries.
metrics_to_monitor: % new model entries that pass tokenizer round-trip (goal >95%)
Median cold-start latency by sequence bucket
% of requests hitting fallback kernels (target <0.5% after promotion)
Incidence of runtime OOMs per model (goal 0 for guarded/pinned models)
Number of forced rollbacks and reason tags
risks: False positives from tokenizer_hash mismatches for tokenizer forks; will require de-dupe/whitelist flow
Overly strict perf gates could block good models—mitigate by pilot and soft warnings for first 2 weeks
Operators may need additional rollback runbooks if models misbehave after promotion
open_questions: Should 'guarded' promotion be time-based, traffic-based, or both? (proposal: require >=1000 requests + 7 days steady)
What exact fallback kernel percentage should block promotion? (proposal: 0.5% threshold provisional)
How do we represent partial compatibility (e.g., model works on A100 but not on Ampere-Lite)? Need per-architecture annotations?
notes: Related: Evals team to provide canonical prompt set for tokenizer round-trip (EVALS-56)
